messages:
Maria: Heads-up — PTQ bring-up for zephyrx-lite (int8) is showing a weird structured-output failure on funcalls. Can reproduce on canary: ~2.3% of calls return non-JSON suffixes (truncated array, stray backslash, or extra \u0000).
Jake: ugh. stack traces / example?
Maria: pasted one minimal example below:
Maria: {"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "redwood inference"}, "meta": {"id": 12345}}
...output continued: 
"results": ["doc1", "doc2"



"
Maria: note the missing closing bracket and then a few NUL chars at the end.
Sudhanshu: is this only on streaming or also full-response?
Maria: both, but streaming amplifies it — we see mid-stream truncation more often. non-ptq float32 run is fine (<0.1%).
ml-bot: telemetry: canary zephyrx-lite-int8 10k calls — parse_fail_rate: 2.31%, first_byte_latency P50: 120ms, p95: 450ms, median tokens: 48. affected endpoints: /invoke-tool (mostly multistep).
Tara: interesting that token length is short. Could be early EOS signaling or kv-cache misalignment after quant kernels. Any recent kernel changes?
Jake: I pushed the int8 kernel reorder patch last week — might be related. Reverting locally drops parse_fail to 0.2% on a small smoke.
Sudhanshu: hypothesis: quant rounding changes produce stray control chars in tokenizer boundary, or trailing padding bytes get serialized when model outputs binary-like tokens. Suggest pipeline: 1) run streaming with a strict sanitization postproc that strips control chars and enforces JSON termination; 2) add suffix sentinel token in prompts; 3) add a targeted canary with mirror (float32) fallback.
Kevin: +1 for mirror fallback. Also propose lowering retry backoff to allow one quick regen before returning a user-visible error — most of these are transient.
Maria: quick patch I tried locally: after collecting stream, run payload = re.sub(r"[\\x00-\\x1F]+$", "", payload) then attempt json.loads with a short rescue that tries to append common terminators like "}]" or "]". Reduced failures to ~0.6% in local. Not perfect.
Tara: can we avoid heuristics that mask real regressions? We should capture raw bytes to S3 for offline analysis and still surface the heuristic-rescued count separately in telemetry.
ml-bot: created ticket INF-PTQ-842 in backlog with sample ids.
Jake: I'll revert the kernel reorder in the canary queue and re-run full 50k sample. If rate drops -> blame kernel. If not -> look at tokenizer/kv-cache interplay.
Sudhanshu: also add a parser-lint in the on-accept gate that flags any rescued outputs so we can compute quality regressions vs golden prompts.
Kevin: timeline?
Maria: Jake will run the 50k re-run today, Sudhanshu will add sanitizer+rescue telemetry, Tara will wire S3 dump for failed raw payloads, and I'll cut canary with mirror fallback (float32 fallback route) by EOD.
Tara: I'll also add an eval that scores funcall precision (schema-accuracy) before/after for the canary.
Maria: ok cool. ping @everyone if anything flaps after revert. :eyes: :shipit:
Jake: on it, posting results in thread when done.
